findings.finding: The six prewritten dispatches each include both Arm A and Arm B instruction sections, whereas protocol.md says each dispatch includes only its arm. The pre-run harness review explicitly required withholding the other arm instructions. The primary agent confirmed that the actual execution plan sent the complete tasks.md with both conditional sections plus an own-arm/workspace prefix.
evidence: dispatches.json, all six records: complete frozen tasks.md suffix and both arm sections
finalize-freeze.mjs, dispatch construction appends the entire tasks.md
primary agent audit-response attestation in this review task; actual opaque plaintext not decrypted
findings.reasoning: Both arms remained operationally separated, but the predeclared arm-specific information restriction was not met. Extra method text is part of a token-cost experiment's input and may affect behavior/context costs. Its irrelevance or zero effect cannot be established without a changed counterfactual; do not retrospectively weaken the protocol because observed command scopes were clean.
findings.adjudication: Do not certify preregistered method conformance or open the summary hard gate. This is not a finding that a candidate accessed the other arm's files, reports or artifacts. Preserve results and disclose the deviation; do not overwrite records, rerun candidates, or relabel the original gate as satisfied.

limits: This is independent adjudication of observable scope and predeclared method, not quality grading or token-efficiency interpretation.
No exact plaintext equivalence or delivery can be proven from opaque persisted dispatch payloads. Prewritten prompts and sender attestation are not cryptographic proof of delivery.
No inherited public history or forked-from identity was observed; no-fork configuration is additionally corroborated by public dispatch metadata, not inspection of private/system context.
Final file hashes and observed calls cannot exclude transient changes reverted before audit, invisible platform actions, or unrecorded external activity; this is not a security sandbox.
MCP runtime/dependency hashes and approved bridge path were verified; this review does not monitor network syscalls or attest every child process binary independently.
Delivery proof uses multiplicity-aware substring consumption, not protocol call-id causal binding. Numeric telemetry and grading remain separate.
Only the six mapped completed sessions are audited; the findings do not certify absence of any undisclosed, unmapped infrastructure run.
The helper was added after completion solely for read-only audit; it is not misrepresented as pre-run instrumentation.
